name: Black Buck Ltd
title: Black Buck Ltd - 544288 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Core revenue up 31% YoY and telematics device sales at record, but vehicle finance break-even reiterated only qualitatively and tolling GTV flat near Rs 7,000 crore; supply-side signals are thin for a capital-cycle read.

summary.headline: BlackBuck Q2 FY27 total income rose about 51% YoY to Rs 253 crore, with PAT up 42% to Rs 41.4 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with revenue from operations up about 56% YoY and net revenue up about 35% to Rs 183 crore. Core business grew 31% YoY, helped by telematics device sales hitting a new high and a 17% rise in tolling GTV to about Rs 7,070 crore. Growth businesses (loads and vehicle finance) grew about 2.7x YoY, but management stepped up investment in super loads and customer acquisition, so total expenses rose 36% and adjusted EBITDA grew about 29% to Rs 55 crore. Management reiterated that vehicle finance is on track for EBITDA break-even this year.

segments.name: Core business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 31% YoY and about 11% QoQ; management said matured lines grow at high teens to about 20%, with telematics the main driver of the QoQ growth. Contribution margin stays well above 90%.

segments.name: Telematics
segments.commentary: Record new device sales for a second straight quarter. Revenue lags sales because it is recognised over time, and deferred revenue grew 56% YoY. Management attributed most of the acceleration to AIS mandates across states, with fuel sensor and dash cam still in pilot.

segments.name: Tolling / payments
segments.commentary: GTV up 17% YoY to about Rs 7,070 crore, with a significant uptick in BlackBuck-issued FASTags through its PPI entity (BlackBuck TZF). Management said incremental FASTags are on its own PPI licence, not replacing partner tags.

segments.name: Growth businesses (loads and vehicle finance)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 2.7x (+166%) YoY and about 25% QoQ. Super loads now run in 14 cities (2 older, 12 newer), and vehicle finance is a partner-led model targeting EBITDA break-even this year.

guidance_outlook: Vehicle finance is on track to reach EBITDA break-even in FY27, per management.
Q3 and Q4 are typically the seasonal pick-up for tolling; October movement was described as business as usual.
Telematics growth expected to continue faster, with AIS tailwinds, and revenue to follow device sales through deferred revenue.
Depreciation expected to rise with telematics growth; management gave no formal guidance.
Super loads investment to continue until the playbook and unit economics are clearer; no capex guidance given.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 771 million was cited by an analyst; management did not comment on the figure or on FY27 capex guidance.
Super loads operate in 14 cities, a cash-and-carry model with advances from customers and very few days of working capital.
Distribution network of about 10,000 touchpoints, present in about 80% of districts.
demand_pricing: Q2 is seasonally weak due to rains; Q1 was hit by an oil-price shock and slower movement, and Q2 partly recovered that.

Management said more than 50% of tolling transactions are below Rs 2,000 and that the PDN route covers the rest, so the UPI MDR impact should be close to zero, though this is untested until implementation.
Pilots in early October broadly followed that pattern, per the CFO.

Telematics pricing is Rs 3,000-4,000 a year versus OEM renewals of Rs 7,000-10,000 per an analyst's fleet-owner checks; management said GPS is optional and customers prefer BlackBuck's bundled software.
Tolling take rate unchanged QoQ apart from minor one-off benefits.

qa_highlights.question: How should tolling GTV (around Rs 6,800-7,000 crore for 3-4 quarters) grow in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is typically a seasonal dip of a few percent QoQ, Q3 and Q4 are the industry pick-up, and October is tracking as business as usual.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new FASTags on BlackBuck's own PPI licence incremental or replacing existing ones, and what does that mean for MDR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner model remains the majority, and new issuance on its own PPI is incremental, with a significant uptick in BlackBuck FASTags.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDR exposure on UPI for tolling on Rs 7,000 crore GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 50% of transactions are below Rs 2,000 and the PDN route covers the rest, so the impact should be close to zero, though the CFO said actual impact will only be clear after implementation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ core growth despite flat GTV and about 2% fewer tolling transactions?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said telematics was the main driver through record device sales, with only minor one-off tolling benefits and no material take-rate change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation trajectory and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said depreciation tracks telematics growth, with deferred revenue up 56% YoY, and gave no formal capex or depreciation guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM bundled GPS subscriptions at lower renewal prices hurt telematics growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GPS is not mandated, repeat buyers already use BlackBuck software, and AIS device activation needs state-level integrations that OEMs are not doing.

qa_highlights.question: Where is opex investment going between tolling and telematics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said upfront customer acquisition costs are expensed in the quarter of strong sales growth and recovered over customer lifetime, which suppresses EBITDA in those quarters.

risks_watch: Adjusted EBITDA is blended with new-business investment; management has not yet split out the segment figures.
UPI MDR changes for FASTag and the PDN adoption rate by customers paying above Rs 2,000.
Dependence on AIS mandates for telematics acceleration, and possible OEM bundled subscription pricing.
Rising depreciation tied to telematics device growth; no guidance given.
Super loads investment and operating leverage (around 50%) versus the historical 70-85%, with the vehicle finance break-even timeline at risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on core growth, telematics and AIS tailwinds, but noticeably less specific on guidance, depreciation, capex and the super loads investment payback. Management leaned on the "business as usual" framing and deferred several numbers, such as the telematics and segment splits, to later disclosures.
key_quotes: Because of a very high market share, largely our pattern would also be indexed to how the market will work.
The large part of the acceleration is because of AIS mandates happening across states for various different use cases.
Currently, there is no guidance on how it will pan out.
We have seen significant uptick in productivities of people and of the cost we are investing in existing cities.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 56% growth YoY (absolute figure not stated)

financial_highlights.metric: Power users (use more than two services)

adds.what: Super loads expansion to 14 cities (12 newer cities added), cash-and-carry model with customer advances

growth.why: Management guided only to vehicle finance EBITDA break-even in FY27 and telematics growth continuing faster with AIS tailwinds; backing is partial (record device sales, 17% GTV growth, 14 super-load cities) with no numeric revenue guidance and no capex or capacity timeline given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Super loads and customer acquisition spend rose, total expenses +36% YoY vs revenue from operations +56%, and adjusted EBITDA grew only ~29% to Rs 55 crore; operating leverage is about 50% vs historical 70-85%, and management expects depreciation to rise with telematics.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Super loads already expanded to 14 cities (12 newly added) and a ~10,000-touchpoint network covers ~80% of districts, but no new capacity timeline or capex was guided and management did not comment on the ~Rs 771 million capex figure cited by an analyst.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Tolling GTV grew 17% YoY to ~Rs 7,070 crore with Q3/Q4 seasonal pick-up flagged and October 'business as usual'; telematics device sales hit records for a second straight quarter, with deferred revenue up 56% YoY and transacting customers up 13% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management gave no capex guidance and did not comment on FY27 capex; super loads run on a cash-and-carry model with very few days of working capital, so no clear capex trigger is in the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance to raise, and the only explicit guide is vehicle finance EBITDA break-even in FY27, which was held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vehicle finance break-even in FY27 is at risk given super loads investment is continuing with no clear payback timeline, and Q2 EBITDA grew only ~29% against revenue +56%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fuel sensor and dash cam telematics are still in pilot with no launch date, and super loads are being extended into more cities, but no firm product timeline was given.

rows.label: AIS mandates driving telematics acceleration
rows.why: Management attributed most of the telematics acceleration to state-level AIS mandates, with record device sales for a second straight quarter and telematics revenue following device sales via deferred revenue (+56% YoY).

rows.label: UPI MDR impact on tolling payments
rows.why: Management said over 50% of tolling transactions are below Rs 2,000 and the PDN route covers the rest, so impact should be near zero on ~Rs 7,070 crore GTV, but this is untested until implementation.

rows.label: Operating leverage recovery in super loads and acquisition spend
rows.why: Upfront customer acquisition costs are expensed in strong-growth quarters and recovered over customer lifetime, with operating leverage around 50% now versus 70-85% historically, so margins could recover only if spend normalises.

tone.note: Management was confident on core tolling and telematics growth and AIS tailwinds, but was vague on guidance, depreciation, capex and super loads payback; analysts pressed on the UPI MDR exposure, the FASTag PPI mix, OEM bundled GPS pricing and the margin drag from investment.
